title: Service Safety: sprint proposal & stakeholder fabrics
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working proposal for a focused 6-week pilot ("Safety Net Sprint") to embed SLO-backed reliability controls into two product teams and the platform stack. Goal: prove a light, repeatable process for cross-team SLO adoption that reduces user-visible incidents and shrinks mean time to remediation for model-serving regressions.

Why this format?
- Drive smaller, measurable experiments (not a big org rewrite).
- Use stakeholder fabrics (named partner contacts + simple handoffs) rather than org-wide mandates.
- Keep runbooks minimal and automatable; focus on detection & fast rollback.

Scope (what's in / out)
- In: two candidate services (hosted-api edge route + dedicated inference pool controller), SLO candidate metrics (p95 latency, token-error-rate, 5m availability), light canary gating, automated error-budget alerts, incident playbook drafts.
- Out: wholesale SLA/legal changes, infra migrations, long-lived quotas or billing changes.

Primary success metrics (experiments must move at least one):
1) Time-to-detect (TTD) for regressions in candidate routes reduced by >=30%
2) Rolling rollback or fallback triggered automatically for at least one staged canary
3) Teams have a working, 1-page runbook and a scheduled 2-week cadence review with SREs
4) Error-budget-aware routing policy proof-of-concept demoed in staging

Stakeholders and roles (fabric contacts)
- Product-hosted-api: Ava Chen (product owner), Diego Morales (backend lead)
- Dedicated capacity: Samir Patel (infra/platform lead), Claire Donovan (capacity planner)
- Serving runtime: Luis Ortega (runtime engineer)
- SRE lead / facilitator: Priya Nair (owner of this pilot)
- Observability: Maya Singh (tracing/alerts)

Working assumptions and constraints
- We will use existing telemetry (prometheus, tracing) and add 3 small derived metrics in the serving runtime if required.
- Canary rollout tooling exists but needs a small adapter layer to tie canary results to error budgets.
- No additional GPU capacity will be purchased for the pilot — use non-peak windows in staging and low-priority queues for experiments.

High-level plan (6 weeks)
Week 0 (prep, pre-sprint): identify routes, owners, and baseline metrics (TTD, TTR, availability). Quick run of previous incidents to map common failure modes.
Week 1: finalize SLO targets with product partners; instrument missing metrics; agree on threshold semantics (p95, error-rate windows).
Week 2: implement lightweight canary gating for route A (hosted-api); create a 1-page rollback playbook per service; wiring of alert -> oncall flow.
Week 3: smoke test canary in staging; run a controlled fault-injection (latency spike) and measure end-to-end detection & rollback.
Week 4: iterate on thresholds, add error-budget signal to routing adapter; start canary for dedicated controller in staging.
Week 5: pilot an automated fallback: route to compatible lower-cost model variant when error-budget or latency SLO breached; run review with exec stakeholders, collect adoption blockers.
Week 6: retro, decision: adopt/process generalization + handoff plan to platform team for next 90 days.

Deliverables by the end of sprint
- Baseline metric snapshot and incident retro summary (pdf/notes)
- Two 1-page runbooks (hosted-api route, dedicated controller)
- Canary gating adapter prototype and demo (github PR)
- Short playbook for error-budget routing with decision matrix
- Retrospective with acceptance decisions and backlog for follow-up work

Design details / experiment templates
- Experiment A: Canary + latency SLO
  - Signal: p95 latency on route, 1-minute rolling window
  - Threshold: p95 > 750ms for 3 consecutive windows -> mark canary unhealthy
  - Action: automated rollback to previous model build (or route to fallback model variant), page team if rollback fails
  - Measurement: TTD, time-to-rollback, number of false positives in 2-week window

- Experiment B: Error-budget routing
  - Signal: error-budget burn rate > 2x across 30m window or >100 errors/min
  - Action: reduce new traffic to variant or shift traffic to dedicated pre-warmed pool; record decision in audit log
  - Measurement: success rate of fallback and impact on user-visible errors

Telemetry / observability checklist (quick wins)
- Ensure p95, p99 histograms exported for both token-level latencies and request-level latencies
- Add a derived metric token_error_rate per route (errors per 1k tokens)
- Hook alerts into #sre-stability and PagerDuty routing for the pilot oncall shift
- Create a dashboard with: baseline, canary snapshot, error-budget burn chart, top failure signatures

Runbook sketch (1 page)
- When alert fires: who to page, what to check (recent deploys, model version, slow nodes), quick mitigation steps (rollback, scale-up pool, route to fallback), post-mortem owner, tags to add, next steps if rollback unsuccessful.

Risk & mitigation table (notes)
- Risk: noisy metric causes oscillation -> Mitigation: require sustained windows + add hysteresis to adapter
- Risk: rollback not possible if model artifact missing -> Mitigation: ensure previous model artifacts retained for 48h post-deploy
- Risk: cascading capacity pressure during fallback -> Mitigation: circuit-breaker thresholds and soft limit on fallback percentage

Dependencies and blockers
- Runtime change: export token_error_rate (owner: Luis) — estimated 2d work
- Canary adapter: small PR to routing service (owner: Diego/Samir) — 3d work
- Observability tweaks: dashboard + alert rules (owner: Maya) — 2d work
- PD runbook sync: require oncall calendar update for pilot window (owner: SRE ops)

Communication plan
- Weekly 30m sync with product & platform partners (Mon 10am)
- Mid-sprint demo (end of week 3) to show canary rollback in staging
- #sre-stability pinned notes with short status updates (twice weekly)

Acceptance criteria for roll to broader program
- Proven reduction in median TTD in at least one candidate (>=30%)
- Canary gating adapter merged and deployed to staging with tests
- Two runbooks ready and 1 pilot oncall trained on playbooks
- Clear backlog with owners and an executive summary for the reliability steering committee

Open questions (to resolve in week 0/1)
- Do product teams accept the proposed SLO windows? (Ava to confirm)
- Are there any regulatory constraints for automatic rollback in customer-dedicated deployments? (legal check)
- Which model variants are safe to be used as fallbacks (quality guardrails)? (product/ML)

Next steps (immediate)
- Owner (Priya): schedule kickoff, create pilot JIRA epic (JIRA-4521) and invite fabric leads
- Diego/Luis: quick spike to estimate runtime metric export effort
- Maya: copy of existing dashboards and proposed new panels
- All partners: review runbook skeleton and add 3 missing checks by EOD Fri

Notes to self / running transcript (informal)
- Keep experiments small. If we try to standardize everything at once we won't ship.
- Focus on actuation (not just observing) — detection without action is an ops tax.
- Document these templates so product teams can replicate the pilot in 30-60m setup time.

If you want to be added as a collaborator or have specific data to include (incident logs, traces), ping me or drop notes into the linked confluence page.

-- Priya
